answer: Candidate rovers in an orchard prove physical authenticity to an aerial auditor via optical telemetry. The overhead auditor records nadir video while challenging each unit to reflect synchronized flashes with a steerable mirror. Since geometry ties each reflection to a unique physical location, scaling fake identities requires fabricating dedicated motorized platforms. However, dense canopy foliage and overcast skies often attenuate the beam, mistakenly rejecting valid machines.
